definitions.explanation: A company other than one's own. Used in business contexts to refer to rival companies, partner companies, or simply any other company.

examples.japanese: {他社|たしゃ}の{製品|せいひん}と{比較|ひかく}した。
examples.english: I compared it with other companies' products.

examples.japanese: {他社|たしゃ}に{先駆|さきが}けて{新商品|しんしょうひん}を{発売|はつばい}した。
examples.english: We released the new product ahead of our competitors.

examples.japanese: {他社|たしゃ}との{差別化|さべつか}を{図|はか}るために、サービスの{質|しつ}を{向上|こうじょう}させた。
examples.english: We improved service quality in order to differentiate ourselves from other companies.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of {他|た} (other) + {社|しゃ} (company). A standard business term used to refer to any company other than one's own. Does not necessarily imply competition — can also refer to partner companies or companies in unrelated industries.

NOTE ON HOMOPHONES:
Not to be confused with {他者|たしゃ} (another person, the other), which uses a different second kanji.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {他社|たしゃ}{製品|せいひん} (other companies' products)
- {他社|たしゃ}との{比較|ひかく} (comparison with other companies)
- {他社|たしゃ}に{負|ま}けない (not to lose to competitors)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {競合他社|きょうごうたしゃ}: competing company — specifically a rival
- {自社|じしゃ}: one's own company — the opposite
